title-group.article-title: Subtree eviction for structured prompts in small language models

abstract.p: Long prompts often contain structure that a model never needs all at once. We store each subtree of a document under its own sequence and remove whole subtrees from the key-value cache when they are no longer needed.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Retrieval systems paste whole documents into a prompt, yet most questions concern a single section. Keeping every token in the cache wastes memory on small devices.

sec.title: Method
sec.p: Each node of the parsed document gets its own sequence identifier, and every token is tagged with the identifiers of its node and all descendants. Siblings therefore cannot attend to each other.
To evict a subtree we remove its identifiers over its position range; the freed cells are reused by later tokens.

sec.title: Experiments
sec.p: We evaluated the method on 120 documents from four domains using a 1-billion-parameter model on a laptop CPU.
Evicting unused subtrees reduced cache memory by 38 percent on average while answer accuracy stayed within one point of the full prompt.

sec.title: Conclusion
sec.p: Structured sequence identifiers make cache eviction safe at the granularity of document sections.
